content.thinking: I'm treating this as a state divergence where the cache has gone stale, with io-summary-cache as the likely subject even though nothing has changed. I'll keep internal-dependency-failure with that same service as a fallback explanation, but I'm checking state divergence first.

hypotheses.subject: io-summary-cache
hypotheses.summary: The cached spend totals (io-summary-cache) stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger from 2026-11-10T03:18:00Z and began being served stale at 2026-11-10T06:12:30Z. The ledger is correct and only the derived copy is behind. No deploy, flag or placement change was recorded.

supporting_evidence.claim: 90 of 240 cached spend figures disagree with the purchases behind them. The purchases are correct and the cached copies are behind; the oldest unaccounted purchase was recorded at 2026-11-10T03:18:00Z and the copies were served from 2026-11-10T06:12:30Z.
get_changes returned nothing changed from 2026-11-09T06:12:30Z to 2026-11-10T06:17:31Z. All three pods started 2026-11-09T18:17:30Z on the same V100 card.
The service register lists io-summary-cache as an internal cache holding the shopper's spend figure, optional by design.

hypotheses.subject: io-summary-cache
hypotheses.summary: The internal io-summary-cache service, owned by checkout-platform, failed to apply updates and so served stale totals.

supporting_evidence.claim: The register shows io-summary-cache is internal and owned by checkout-platform. The alert says nothing is putting the copies right.
